name: pivot_camarilla_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Camarilla pivot points, derived from the previous day's OHLC using specific multipliers (1.1/12, 1.1/6, 1.1/4, 1.1/2), create 8 intraday support/resistance levels (S1-S4, R1-R4) that are more tightly clustered around the previous close than standard pivot points. The key Camarilla trade: price bouncing between S3/R3 levels (mean reversion zone) accounts for ~65% of trading days, while S4/R4 breakouts signal trend days (~35%). In Indian markets, Camarilla levels work particularly well because: (1) the previous close anchors retail trader sentiment heavily (Indian retail psychology fixates on daily P&L), (2) institutional VWAP algorithms naturally create support/resistance near these mathematically derived levels, (3) the S3/R3 bounce is a self-fulfilling prophecy — Indian technical analysis channels widely teach Camarilla, creating order flow at these levels.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents + NIFTY 50 / BANK NIFTY index

other: previous day OHLC for pivot computation

indicators.name: cam_zone
indicators.formula: 'range' if close between cam_S3 and cam_R3; 'breakout_up' if close > cam_R4; 'breakout_down' if close < cam_S4; 'transition' otherwise

conditions: (cam_zone == 'range' AND close <= cam_S3 * 1.001) — bouncing at S3 support
OR (cam_zone == 'breakout_up' AND close > cam_R4) — breakout above R4 (trend day)
close > low of last 3 bars (for S3 bounce) OR volume surge (for R4 breakout)
long.confirmation: S3 bounce: close > cam_S3 AND close > close[1]. R4 breakout: close > cam_R4 for 2 bars with volume > 1.5x average

conditions: (cam_zone == 'range' AND close >= cam_R3 * 0.999) — rejecting at R3 resistance
OR (cam_zone == 'breakout_down' AND close < cam_S4) — breakdown below S4
close < high of last 3 bars (for R3 rejection) OR volume surge (for S4 breakdown)
short.confirmation: R3 rejection: close < cam_R3 AND close < close[1]. S4 breakdown: close < cam_S4 for 2 bars with volume > 1.5x average

entry.entry_price: limit at S3/R3 level (bounce trades), market order (breakout trades)

exit.target: S3 bounce → target cam_R3 (full range traverse). R4 breakout → 20 bps beyond R4.
exit.stop_loss: S3 bounce → below S4 (support broken). R4 breakout → back below R3 (false breakout).
exit.trailing_stop: 10 bps trailing for breakout trades after 15 bps profit
exit.time_stop: exit after 45 bars (range trades); 30 bars (breakout trades)
exit.signal_exit: cam_zone changes (transition between range and breakout mode)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade. Increase to ₹1.5L for breakout trades with volume confirmation.

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 for range trades (S3/R3 bounce). No VIX filter for breakout trades.
filters.time_filter: no range trades first 5 min; breakout trades can start immediately
filters.volume_filter: breakout trades require volume > 1.5x average at breakout bar
filters.trend_filter: range trades: NIFTY range-bound. Breakout trades: NIFTY trending in breakout direction
filters.event_filter: prefer range trades on non-event days; breakout trades on event days
other_filters: skip if previous day range was < 0.3% (Camarilla levels too tight, no room for trades)
skip if gap > S4 or R4 at open (levels already breached by gap)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — Camarilla pivots are well-known among Indian retail traders. The edge is in correctly identifying range vs breakout days (which most traders don't do) and the self-fulfilling prophecy at S3/R3 levels.

weaknesses: On gap-up/gap-down days (opening beyond S4/R4), Camarilla levels are already breached and provide no useful structure for the day.
The 65/35 range/breakout day split is an average — in volatile regimes (VIX > 20), breakout days may dominate, and the range strategy will generate consecutive losses.
Camarilla levels are static (computed from previous day) and don't adapt to intraday price discovery. VWAP-based dynamic levels may be more appropriate.
prior_art: Nick Stott — original Camarilla equation (1989). Pivot point trading methodology is covered in Murphy (1999) 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets'. In India, Camarilla pivots are featured on moneycontrol.com and are standard on Zerodha Kite charts.
notes: Compute Camarilla levels before market open using previous day's OHLC data. The levels are fixed for the entire session. The key decision is early: is today a range day (trade S3/R3 bounces) or a trend day (trade S4/R4 breakouts)? India VIX level and gap size at open are useful predictors of day type.
